Description: A lengthy Hebrew copy of Numbers from Qumran Cave 4, published in DJD XII (Jastram). Remains of 27 columns survive, covering Numbers 11-36 in fragments, written in early Herodian semiformal Hebrew script. A few lines are written in red ink. It is one of only a handful of Qumran biblical manuscripts with over 1,000 words preserved.
Significance: The fullest Numbers witness from Qumran, and an expansionist-type text: many of its variants agree with the Greek Septuagint against the Masoretic Text, demonstrating that differing versions of Numbers circulated in the Second Temple period. It is the standard comparison text for Numbers textual criticism at Qumran.
